string-array.item: How can I tell the developer what I think?
How are notes, reminders, habits, and goals classified?
Why can\'t I manually set a thing as a reminder, habit, or goal?
What permissions does EverythingDone need, and why?
Why does a new thing appear after I finish everything, and why can\'t I swipe it away? My OCD is about to cry.
Can I see statistics about reminders and habits?
Why didn\'t my completion rate change after I deleted a thing?
Why can habits remind me at most 4 times per day? Why can\'t I set reminders like several times every few cycles?
Why do completed and created notes count toward the completion-rate formula, while habit completions in each cycle do not?
Why is there no sync feature yet?
Will there be more thing colours?
Why is the lunar calendar not supported?
Why are image attachment thumbnails cropped poorly, and why are large images not clear enough?
Are there any easter eggs in EverythingDone? (,,• ₃ •,,)

string-array.name: help_contents
string-array.item:
First, I want this page to answer questions you may have while using EverythingDone, so the problems you run into can be solved as quickly as possible. 

Second, people are different, and a developer's ideas may differ a lot from a user's. I also want to use this page to explain the thinking behind some EverythingDone settings: what I was considering when I designed those features. Some of that thinking may be different from yours, and some of it may even look silly, but those ideas are exactly what give this app its own shape. I hope you can understand them and enjoy that difference and change. 

This page will keep being updated.

Note: record moments in life, such as a person, an event, or a scene, without setting any reminder. 

Reminder: EverythingDone reminds you of the thing, and that reminder should happen within 4 weeks (28 days) after the thing is created. 

Habit: EverythingDone repeatedly reminds you of the thing. The repeat cycle can be a day, a week, a month, or a year, and the number of repeats depends on the cycle type. 

Goal: EverythingDone reminds you of the thing, and that reminder should happen at least 4 weeks after the thing is created. This kind of thing usually requires long-term effort to complete.

The main reason is that I want you to focus only on the thing itself, not spend extra time and energy deciding what type it should be. You only need to tell EverythingDone when you want to be reminded (whether that means when to start doing it or when it should be finished; I do not distinguish those two cases, and that should not affect the nature of the thing) and whether the reminder should be one-time or repeated. EverythingDone will then decide the type from that information: reminders are short-term, habits are repetitive, and goals are long-term. \n\nAnother reason is that if manual type changes were allowed now, many errors would appear throughout the app. So even if users ask for this feature, I would need to redesign the whole app structure and rewrite a lot of code. Before EverythingDone 2.0, I probably will not want to do that.

If your system is a third-party Android system such as MIUI, flyme, or EMUI, please grant EverythingDone all the permissions it needs. Make sure EverythingDone can start after boot, keep running in the background, start itself from the background, and show notification messages. If your phone has a built-in power-saving assistant, such as EMUI, please also go to its settings and add EverythingDone to the whitelist. 

If you use phone optimisation or cleanup apps such as 360 Mobile Assistant or Greenify, please also make sure EverythingDone is not included in their optimisation or cleanup scope. 

If you have installed notification-management apps such as Nevolution or 360 Notification Box, please add EverythingDone to their whitelists as well, so notifications do not disappear. 

If you still cannot receive reminders, please send me feedback and include your phone model, system type, and version number. I will contact you for more details. 

Many ROMs today, especially well-localised ones, want to control every behaviour of third-party apps. This is a strong protection against malicious apps. EverythingDone is not a malicious app, but those manufacturers do not know that and will not make an exception for me. As a result, EverythingDone's reminder feature may be affected to some extent. Please understand both me and those manufacturers.

After all things of a certain type are completed, there should be a congratulation prompt. In my design, this feature is implemented by automatically creating a new thing. 

Without this thing, the interface would look very empty. Also, because text such as "Underway" sits near the vertical centre of the screen instead of at the top, it would be harder to balance the interface. Designing an empty-state prompt is difficult too: it has to match the app's style, feel fresh and pleasant, and fit the specific empty state, such as everything being completed on the Underway page or no thing being completed on the Finished page. That is challenging and takes quite a bit of time. 

Finally, changing this design now would also require many changes to the app code, which is another laborious task. So I can only ask everyone with OCD to understand... 

Actually, I have OCD too!

Yes. Open the app drawer and tap the image at the top to enter the statistics screen. There you can see how long you have used EverythingDone, how many words you have written, the average reminder time, the habit development rate, and more.

In general, the completion-rate formula is: completed things (not including habit completions inside each cycle) / created things. Even if you delete a thing, the fact that it was created does not change, so the completion rate does not change.

At first I imagined letting you enter how many reminders should happen every few cycles, but that introduces an important question: exactly when should the reminders happen? Should you enter the exact time of every reminder, or should EverythingDone decide when to remind you? 

In the first case, you would need to enter a lot of information, and it is hard to make that input standard. For example, if you want a reminder once every 3 days, on which day and at what time within those 3 days should the reminder happen? How should you express that expectation to EverythingDone? 

In the second case, I cannot intelligently decide when the reminder should happen. Besides, because of Android limitations, I can only set the interval of each repeated reminder to the same duration. That means the reminder times can only be evenly divided, and they certainly will not always be the most appropriate times. Even without repeated reminders, if the app dynamically calculated the next reminder time after each reminder, it would still be hard to decide which time is suitable. 

So for now I only provide reminder forms such as several times per day, week, month, or year. For the more flexible Daily type, I also limit you to at most 4 reminders. Why 4? Because at the time I thought people take medicine at most 4 times a day... This reason may not be very strong, but as I said, it forms part of EverythingDone's unique shape and probably will not change in the foreseeable future.

Sometimes we casually write down things we need to do, but do not know when they should be finished. That is why I decided to include the number of notes in the completion-rate formula. 

The second issue is this: if you only have one thing, and that thing is a habit, then no matter how many times you complete it, your overall completion rate will not increase unless you develop that habit. In fact, in my original design, habit completions in each cycle were counted in the completion-rate formula. But then fully developing a habit, which is a very important action, would not have a matching effect on the completion rate, so I later changed it to the current formula. 

Of course, if you want to know the real completion rate of habits, you can check the statistics screen; if you want to know the completion rate of a specific habit, you can also see it on that habit's detail screen.
For a note and reminder app, synchronising notes is indeed very important. But because the developer is still not strong enough, it will take some time to finish. I hope you can understand.

The design draft had two palettes, soft and calm, but choosing the colours for the calm palette alone took almost a week... 

If more softer colours are added now, I also have to consider how they coordinate with existing colours, how fonts and dialogs should match them, and how to avoid making the interface look dazzling because of too many colours. 

Green and purple were added in version 1.2.2, orange and red were added in version 1.3.5, and more colours may be provided through multiple themes in the future.

For me right now, the algorithm for determining the lunar date of a particular day is too deep and difficult; for users, entering a lunar date is also troublesome. Adding the lunar calendar is one of the rare things where I feel I do not know where to start, so you can look forward to whether this feature can be added within 10 years.

Images differ from each other. Some have their main subject in the centre, while others have it near the edges. The program cannot judge that, so I can only honestly show the centre part of the image in the thumbnail. \n\nLarge images are not clear enough because loading the original image consumes many resources, and Android does not allow one app to consume most of the phone hardware. So I can only compress the original image while trying to lose as little detail as possible. But this compression algorithm is the system\'s native one. It is not like apps such as QuickPic, which have their own specialised algorithms, so it is hard to achieve the optimal result.
I deliberately placed three easter eggs. If you find all of them, you can contact me and I will send you a prize~ \n\nWell, you will never find them all. Hahahahahahaha.

resources.string: Click menu button, you will see Undo and Redo there. Now you can let your things back to past or future at any time if you want.
There will be more noticeable notification for things\' alarms. If you are ready, you can start doing the thing directly after the notification, EverythingDone will help you finish it carefully.
Start doing something at any time, or automatically

Now, you can swipe a thing card to right to start doing that thing at any time.\n\nBesides, now you can also enable auto starting doing the thing when its reminder is coming, with another new function, auto entering strict mode, EverythingDone can help you stop saying \"do it later\" any more.
Save edits automatically and change habit records

Now you can enable saving edits automatically when creating or updating a thing. \n\nYou can also change your latest habit records to correct mistakes or pick lost memory. Check a habit, open menu, click \"check habit detail\" and you will see that action.
